correctness.rationale: Conjugate the right-shore bits to make a neighbor-majority process with a flip on ties. When n odd, one shore has at least its pivotal majority threshold, and a sequence of permitted updates drives all vertices to one polar state. When n even and t<n, all cases except balanced a=b=n/2 likewise polarize; an undeleted-index vertex at the balanced point has an exact tie and can flip to exit this case. Hence every state reaches one of two absorbing states. When n even,t=n all degrees are odd, every actual flip strictly raises the cut and recurrent states are precisely fixed points; the two-shore inequalities force either a polarization or opposite bits across each deleted pair and exactly n/2 positive indices, giving C(n,n/2). Independent direct enumeration for n=3..6, all t, computed all stable configurations and reverse reachable sets from them; every state reaches the claimed absorbing set. This bounded check does not prove all n.
residual_risks: Tie retention in the original closed-neighborhood minority rule and tie-flipping in the dual majority rule are essential and not interchangeable with Nash ties accepted.
No absorption-time distribution, noisy dynamics or arbitrary edge deletion classification.

originality.rationale: Rouquier–Regnault–Thierry established foundational asynchronous minority, energy and bipartite duality, but their studied examples do not include this complete matching-deletion threshold. A separate published same-graph anti-coordination Nash-census theorem counts weak Nash equilibria and recovers the even full-deletion binomial number; this overlap is explicitly credited. For partially deleted matching, weak equilibria with ties are not absorbing under the required tie-flip dynamics, so that static theorem does not imply only two recurrent classes or almost-sure absorption. The sharp dynamic restoration theorem survives under bounded comparisons.
residual_risks: Specialized exact stochastic anti-coordination/crown-graph analyses may exist under different terminology.
The same-graph static Nash census already covers full-matching equilibrium counts, not independently new at t=n.
No rate of absorption is provided; finite-state reachability establishes almost sure absorption only.

value.rationale: A natural interpolation between a complete bipartite network and a crown graph has a sharp last-edge change in zero-noise asynchronous dynamics. Restoring a single edge eliminates exponentially many suboptimal absorbing configurations that retain only about half of the maximum cut. The distinction from weak local Nash stability is mathematically substantive for tie-sensitive dynamics and motivates the exact recurrence-free classification.
residual_risks: Homogeneous unweighted graph and a specified tie-preserving original update rule only.
